cases.standard:
No license under any patent, trademark, copyright, or other intellectual
property right is granted or implied by this Agreement.
cases.alternative:
Nothing herein grants the Receiving Party any rights, by license or otherwise, in
or to any intellectual property of the Disclosing Party.
cases.generated_prose: Alternative limits the license grant to the Receiving Party and the Disclosing Party's intellectual property, whereas the standard applies a mutual no-license prohibition to all intellectual property rights under the agreement.

cases.standard:
The Receiving Party shall protect the Confidential Information using at least the same
degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential and proprietary
information of similar nature and importance, but in no event less than reasonable
care.
cases.alternative:
The Receiving Party agrees to: (a) hold the Confidential Information in confidence and use
reasonable care to prevent its unauthorized use, disclosure, or duplication;
cases.generated_prose: Standard of care reduced from the greater of customary or reasonable care to reasonable care only.

cases.standard:
Each Party irrevocably consents
to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware
for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
cases.alternative:
The Parties consent to exclusive jurisdiction
in the Delaware Court of Chancery (or, if such court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction, the
federal courts located in Delaware).
cases.generated_prose: Consent to exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery or federal courts in Delaware instead of state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware.

cases.standard:
Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes generally
available to the public through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was in the Receiving Party's

lawful possession prior to disclosure and not subject to any prior confidentiality obligation;
(c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to the Confidential
Information, as demonstrated by competent written records; or (d) is rightfully obtained from
a third party not in breach of any confidentiality obligation.
cases.generated_prose: If the contract narrows these exclusions or omits specific categories (e.g., independent development or public availability), insert the four-part standard language to ensure the Receiving Party is not penalized for information that legally does not require protection. Push for explicit requirements such as 'competent written records' for independent development to provide objective verification.
